stories.headline: Alphabet's stock takes a historic tumble
stories.summary: Google's parent company, Alphabet, saw its stock drop 10% in premarket trading, heading for its biggest post-earnings fall ever. This wasn't just a minor hiccup; investors were spooked by a larger-than-expected negative free cash flow, even though the company is sticking to its spending plans for the year. Seems like even tech giants have off days.

stories.headline: Eli Lilly's weight-loss drugs are a cash cow
stories.summary: Good news for Eli Lilly! Their sales absolutely crushed estimates, and they’ve hiked their sales outlook thanks to the unstoppable demand for their obesity drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro. People are really shelling out for these, making them a huge win for the pharma giant.

stories.headline: Poundland teeters on the brink in the UK
stories.summary: Looks like the beloved discount chain Poundland might be in serious trouble, as bosses have filed a notice to appoint administrators. This means the future of the "everything for a pound" store hangs in the balance, a sign of ongoing tough times for UK retail.

stories.headline: North Dakota's "socialist" bank is a Republican favorite
stories.summary: In a surprising twist, North Dakota's state-owned bank, often touted by democratic socialists as a model, is actually quite popular with local Republicans. It's a unique financial institution that's been around for over a century, proving that sometimes, pragmatism trumps political labels, especially when it comes to supporting local businesses and farmers.

stories.headline: UK Budget gets a mixed reception
stories.summary: The latest UK budget has stirred up a lot of feelings, from people on £30,000 salaries angry about no fuel duty cuts, to those earning £126,000 who still feel stretched thin. While government borrowing costs fell and some businesses welcomed relief on rates, the overall sentiment for many households and some sectors seems to be "too little, too late" in the face of persistent high energy prices and living costs.

stories.headline: ECB chief Christine Lagarde stepping down early
stories.summary: Europe's top central banker, Christine Lagarde, is unexpectedly resigning as President of the European Central Bank nine months before her term ends. This is a big deal for the eurozone economy, as the search is now on for a successor to guide monetary policy in a period of ongoing uncertainty.

stories.headline: Spain rocked by second deadly train crash this year
stories.summary: Tragedy has struck Spain again, with a high-speed train slamming into the rear of another, killing dozens and injuring many more. This is the second major rail disaster in the country this year, raising serious questions about the safety and maintenance of Spain’s rail network, especially ahead of a national election.

stories.headline: Flavio Bolsonaro flees Brazil for Miami after election loss
stories.summary: Former Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, son of Jair Bolsonaro, has fled to the U.S. after authorities ordered him to surrender his passport amidst multiple investigations. He's reportedly landed in Miami, following in his father's footsteps, and even declared himself the "leader" of Brazil despite losing the election. It's quite the political drama playing out internationally.

stories.headline: Iran tensions escalate as ship reportedly catches fire off Oman
stories.summary: Fears of military escalation in the Middle East are growing after a ship was reported on fire in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping lane. This comes as Iran claims to have shot down another U.S. drone, further ratcheting up tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both sides making strong statements about negotiations and nuclear programs.

stories.headline: US political battles heat up ahead of midterms
stories.summary: The U.S. political landscape is a full-contact sport right now. Republicans are struggling with public opinion on Iran and gas prices, while House progressives are mapping out an ambitious 2027 wishlist including Medicare for All. Meanwhile, Trump is adding fuel to the fire with accusations of fraud and perjury in tight Senate races, making for a very contentious run-up to the midterms.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu greenlights social justice survey
stories.summary: The PMK party is celebrating after the Tamil Nadu Cabinet gave the nod for a Social Justice Survey, a move they've championed for 47 years. The survey is seen as crucial to safeguarding the state's 69% reservation system and will have significant implications for policy and social equity.

stories.headline: Chennai Mayor disputes CM's monsoon inspection timing
stories.summary: A bit of local political drama brewing in Chennai: the Mayor stated she wasn't informed about the Chief Minister's timing for a Northeast monsoon inspection. This sparked debate, with the Deputy Mayor citing protocol during PM visits to counter social media claims of a deliberate boycott, highlighting local governance tensions.

stories.headline: Ex-MLA Muthukumar surrenders in bribery case
stories.summary: Former MLA Muthukumar has surrendered in a bribery case involving ex-Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, after the Supreme Court dismissed his anticipatory bail petition. This marks a significant development in a high-profile corruption case, underscoring ongoing efforts to tackle graft.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab set to hit Andhra coast
stories.summary: Cyclone Arnab, now weakened but still packing a punch, is expected to bring heavy rains to the Andhra coast. Its remnants have already caused havoc with 300 villages marooned in Ganjam, as authorities brace for a new Bay system that could exacerbate conditions.

stories.headline: Cape Canaveral is booming with rocket launches
stories.summary: Call it the new space race! Cape Canaveral is experiencing a "boom cycle" of rocket launches, now outstripping even the Cold War-era Apollo program. This surge in activity underscores the U.S.'s push to expand rocket providers and strengthen its presence in a competitive space and arms race. It's like Space Mountain is open for business, every day.

stories.headline: US sets new record for battery storage
stories.summary: The U.S. just added a record 20.2 GWh of battery storage in a mere three months. That's a huge leap in energy infrastructure, moving us closer to a more stable, renewable-powered grid. Basically, we're getting way better at saving energy for a rainy (or windless) day.

stories.headline: Apple's new MacBook Pro costs an eye-watering $14,549
stories.summary: If you thought Apple products were expensive before, brace yourself. The new touchscreen MacBook Pro, fully upgraded, will set you back a cool $14,549. It’s pushing laptop pricing to an extreme, making even luxury cars seem affordable by comparison for a computer. Who knew a laptop could require a second mortgage?

stories.headline: Hackers steal over 40,000 DHS employee records
stories.summary: A major cybersecurity breach has hit the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), with a hacker stealing personal information from more than 41,000 employees. This trove of data, including names, job titles, and contact info for ICE and Customs and Border Protection staff, is a serious national security concern and a stark reminder that no organization is fully immune.

stories.headline: Akai embraces "vibe-coded" mods for its new MPC
stories.summary: Music tech company Akai is leaning into the hacker community for its unannounced MPC Sample Key, giving developers early access to an open-source device for "vibe-coded" mods. This is a cool move, fostering creativity and customization for its users, letting the community literally shape the future of their instruments.

stories.headline: The forgotten pioneers of dark matter
stories.summary: Turns out the idea of dark matter, this mysterious non-interacting stuff that dominates our universe, goes all the way back to 1933! While Vera Rubin is often credited with confirming its existence decades later, Swiss astronomer Fritz Zwicky actually proposed it first. It’s a fascinating reminder that scientific discoveries often have a long, winding history with many contributors.

stories.headline: Battling "acedia" in the age of algorithms
stories.summary: Ancient monks had a term, "acedia," for that restless urge to be anywhere but where you are, doing anything but what's in front of you. Today, some argue that algorithms and constant digital distractions are making "acedia" the real casualty of our free will, constantly pulling us away from focus and presence. It makes you wonder how much of your day is truly *yours*.

stories.headline: The cosmic speed limits that keep us grounded
stories.summary: You can see billions of galaxies through a telescope, but just because you can see it doesn't mean you can ever reach it. The expansion of the universe itself sets fundamental limits on how far we can travel, creating "divisions" that dictate what parts of the cosmos are forever beyond our grasp. It's a humbling thought about our place in the vast, ever-expanding void.

stories.headline: AI drones are changing the game in Ukraine
stories.summary: Artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable, and both Russia and Ukraine are deploying them extensively in the war. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy has even warned that AI could be making battlefield decisions as soon as next year. This is a stark look at how AI is not just a tech trend, but a real-world, life-and-death factor in modern conflict.

stories.headline: Microsoft rakes in billions from its AI bets
stories.summary: Microsoft is having a moment, reporting a staggering $10 billion in revenue from its commercial partnerships with OpenAI and sharing its Azure cloud platform brought in $33.2 billion. This isn't just a record quarter; it clearly shows how deeply integrated AI is becoming into Microsoft's core business, proving that their massive investment in the space is paying off big time.

stories.headline: Google pushes AI Search ads globally as growth slows
stories.summary: Google is expanding its AI Search ads worldwide, a move that comes as core ad growth for the company is slowing. This signals that Google is quickly trying to monetize its AI advancements, betting that these smarter, more integrated ads will help them maintain their advertising dominance in an evolving search landscape.

stories.headline: An AI breakthrough might make decades of computer science 'irrelevant'
stories.summary: Hold onto your hats, computer scientists! Leading AI labs Anthropic and OpenAI claim to have disproved a key tenet of computer science. While it sounds dramatic, researchers are reportedly feeling like "overexcited bunnies," grappling with the implications while simultaneously seeing a whole new frontier of questions to explore. Talk about a paradigm shift!

stories.headline: Negativity around AI is expected to get worse
stories.summary: Instagram head Adam Mosseri is bracing for impact, acknowledging that public negativity around AI, already palpable, is "going to get worse." This isn't just about college students booing tech CEOs; it reflects growing unease across society about AI's implications for jobs, ethics, and control. It seems the tech industry knows it has a PR problem on its hands.
